name: choropleth
title: Choropleth map
tagline: Choropleth map from the plate atlas: regions shaded by your data through a derived class scale and key; occlude a value or blank a shade to question it; two panels share one scale.
description: A choropleth map rendered from a base-map plate in the atlas (world countries, Europe, and more), with every region shaded by your data through a DERIVED class scale. You author only the data (region code → number), what the value is called, and the classing choice — equal-interval or quantile, 3 to 7 classes; the class breaks, every region's fill, the graded key bar with its boundary values, the no-data row and the accessible description are all computed, so a shade can never contradict its value. Call-outs mark chosen regions with their name and value: occlude a value for a "read the map" question (the region stays shaded; pupils read its class from the key), or blank a region's shade with the value shown for "complete the map from the data". Two panels on one SHARED scale support compare-two-dates or compare-two-indicators — the same shade means the same range in both maps, which is what makes the comparison honest. "tonal" is the greyscale print scheme. For a labelled diagram of drawn artwork use diagram/annotated-figure; for grid references and relief use geography/map-extract.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a lesson shades a map by data: development indicators (GDP per person, HDI, birth rate), population density, rainfall or climate bands, internet access, any "darker means more" map — reading them, completing them, and describing the distribution. Pick the plate FIRST from the atlas index (world for global patterns; europe for a continent close-up; usa-canada or caribbean for regional studies) and key your data by the codes the index lists. Author the data and the classing; never a colour. Classing: equal-interval (default) suits evenly spread data and is the classing pupils are taught to construct; quantile suits skewed data (population, GDP) — with 5 classes it is the exam-standard look. Keep the classing and class count IDENTICAL across blocks that discuss the same dataset, and put the question in the block text, not on the figure. One caution when you occlude: pick a region in the MIDDLE of the data, never the highest or lowest. The key has to state its own range, so the extreme region's exact value is printed at the end of the bar and the question answers itself. Common configurations: read the map — add the region to `regions` with occlude true and ask for its class or an estimate; complete the map — blank 2–4 regions (their values show in the call-outs) and ask pupils to shade them using the key; identify — display "tag" with letters for "which letter shows…?"; compare two dates — two `panels` with titles, one derived shared scale. valueLabel names the quantity WITH its unit ("Population density (people per km²)") — it heads the key. Values at the key joints display compactly (1.5k, 12M). Set interactive true on web for tap-a-region readouts. Synonyms teachers use: choropleth, shaded map, density map, thematic map, development map, "the darker the colour the higher the…".

plate.description: Which base map to draw, by plate id (e.g. "world", "europe"). See the atlas index for each plate's regions and codes.

plateData.description: The resolved plate. Supplied by the HOST from the plate ref — never authored by hand.

panels.description: The map panel(s). One panel is the normal choropleth. TWO panels stack vertically and share ONE derived class scale computed over both datasets together — the honesty guarantee for compare-two-dates ("Internet access, 2005 vs 2025") or compare-two-indicators. Give each panel a title when there are two.

title.description: Short label above this panel (e.g. "2005"). Optional for a single panel.

data.description: The datum, keyed by region code from the plate — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for country maps (e.g. { "GB": 275, "FR": 118 }), ISO 3166-2 for the usa-canada plate (e.g. "US-TX", "CA-ON"). See the atlas index for each plate's codes. Codes are matched case-insensitively; a region with no entry renders in the fixed no-data grey and the key gains a derived "No data" row. Values are plain numbers in the unit that valueLabel names.

valueLabel.description: What the data IS, with its unit — heads the key ("Population density (people per km²)", "Birth rate (per 1,000 people)").

classes.description: The classing choice. The BREAKS are always derived from the data — there is nowhere to author one. Omit for equal-interval with 5 classes.

method.description: "equal-interval" (default): the range is split into equal-width classes — the classing pupils construct by hand. "quantile": class breaks put (near-)equal numbers of regions in each class — the right choice for skewed data such as population or GDP, where equal-interval would put almost everything in the first class.

count.description: Number of classes. Default 5 — the exam-standard look.

id.description: Region code from the plate (e.g. "BR", "US-TX"). A code the plate does not define is ignored.

display.description: "name" (default) writes the region's name in the call-out. "tag" shows its letter alone — the lettered-map form, for "which letter shows…?" questions (set tag).

tag.description: The letter (A, B, C…) for display "tag".

occlude.description: Render the call-out's value as "?" — the "read the map" question: the region stays shaded, and pupils read its class from the shade and the key. The hidden value is withheld from the accessible description too. Default false.

blank.description: Draw this region UNSHADED (hatched answer space) with its value SHOWN in the call-out — the "complete the map from the data" question: pupils class the value against the key and shade the region. Wins over occlude. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber ring around the region and its call-out — the answer, or the region under discussion. Default false.

regions.description: Regions the question points at. Each gets a call-out (name or letter, plus its value) with a leader line. Occlude for "read the map"; blank for "complete the map"; highlight for emphasis.

key.description: Draw the derived key (graded bar, boundary values, no-data row, valueLabel title). Default true — reading against the key is the skill. Turn off only when the key itself is the thing being constructed in the block text.

scheme.description: "colour" (default): the sequential blue ramp. "tonal": the greyscale print ramp, graded so classes still separate on paper.

interactive.description: Web-only: tap or click a region for a transient readout of its name, value and class. A region whose value is occluded or blank reports its name only — the answer never leaks. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
